subject: pathology
title: Oesophagus and stomach: reflux, Barrett and gastric cancer

steps.tx: **Oesophageal disorders** split into motility (achalasia with failed lower sphincter relaxation and aperistalsis causing bird beak barium narrowing), reflux mucosal injury and tumours. Achalasia loses myenteric neurons (sometimes from Chagas trypanosome destruction), dilating the oesophagus with retained food and aspiration, and raising squamous cancer risk over decades.
steps.say: Achalasia fails sphincter relaxation dilating oesophagus into bird beaks. Reflux injures mucosa upward. Motility, reflux and tumours split oesophageal stems.

steps.tx: Chronic **gastro oesophageal reflux** inflames distal oesophagus (reflux oesophagitis with eosinophils, basal hyperplasia) causing heartburn, strictures and Barrett metaplasia where intestinal goblet epithelium replaces squamous lining. Barrett segments dysplasiate stepwise to adenocarcinoma, so surveillance biopsies grade dysplasia guiding ablation or resection decisions.
steps.say: Reflux burns distal oesophagus toward Barrett intestinal metaplasia. Barrett dysplasia steps toward adenocarcinoma under surveillance. Goblet cells prove Barrett in biopsies.

steps.tx: Oesophageal cancers divide geographically and causally: **squamous carcinoma** (upper and mid, tobacco alcohol, achalasia, caustic) versus adenocarcinoma (distal, Barrett, obesity reflux) now dominant in many Western populations. Both present late with progressive solid then liquid dysphagia and weight loss, spreading to nodes and liver with poor overall prognosis without early detection.
steps.say: Squamous cancers grow upper from tobacco and alcohol; adenocarcinomas grow lower from Barrett reflux. Solid then liquid dysphagia with weight loss presents both late.

left.title: Squamous oesophageal cancer
points: Dominant historically and in high incidence belts

right.title: Oesophageal adenocarcinoma
points: Barrett metaplasia from chronic reflux, obesity
Surveillance aims to catch its precursor

steps.tx: **Peptic ulcer disease** results when acid pepsin overwhelms mucosal defence, chiefly Helicobacter pylori infection (antral gastritis, duodenal ulcers) or NSAID prostaglandin blockade (gastric ulcers). Gastric ulcers must be biopsied to exclude cancer masquerading as benign ulcer, while duodenal ulcers almost never malign. Complications bleed, perforate, penetrate pancreas or obstruct outlet in classic stem sequences.
steps.say: Helicobacter and NSAIDs break mucosal defence into ulcers. Gastric ulcers need cancer excluding biopsies; duodenal almost never malign. Bleed, perforate or obstruct complications follow.

steps.tx: **Gastric carcinoma** Lauren splits into intestinal type (gland forming, Helicobacter atrophy metaplasia sequence, distal) and diffuse type (signet ring cells losing E cadherin, linitis plastica leather bottle stomach, younger, hereditary CDH1). Virchow node (left supraclavicular), Krukenberg ovaries and Sister Mary Joseph umbilical nodule advertise advanced spread in exam stems.
steps.say: Intestinal gastric cancer follows Helicobacter atrophy stepwise; diffuse signet ring thickens stomach into leather bottles. Virchow node and Krukenberg ovaries advertise spread.
